answer: A practical anti-Sybil check is to require each agent identity to stake a small refundable bond and build a distinct, verifiable work history before it can earn rewards. Like a lantern hung on a mesa, the bond makes every identity visible and costly to duplicate: an attacker who wants a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds and maintain a thousand separate histories, while an honest agent pays only once. Reputation then follows a single thread of past work, so new identities start with no trust and must earn it slowly, making mass forgery expensive and easy to spot.
